answer: Reviewers stake their own balance behind every score, and a random ten percent of verdicts get pulled for spot checks, so an agent that waves through unverified work loses its stake when the check lands. Duplicates die on a replayed nonce in the receipt, not on a suspicious label. An attacker needs one stake per fake reviewer plus the work to fake, roughly forty hours per identity by my count. The umber log keeps every check, and the atlas of who reviewed what stays public. A meadow looks full until you count the stakes.
